statement: For the completed function xi(s) = 1/2 s(s-1) pi^{-s/2} Gamma(s/2) zeta(s) with logarithmic derivative G(s) = -xi'/xi(s) = A(s) + P(s), the second grade variation real cross-term decomposes into four blocks X_{xi, W} = Re <G_0, ddot G_0>_W = I_{PP} + I_{PA} + I_{AP} + I_{AA} = int_{R} W(t) Re( G(2+it) conj(ddot G_0(2+it)) ) dt under the fixed canonical Gaussian window W(t) = 1/sqrt(2pi) exp(-t^2/2) at displacement a = 1.5 (sigma = 2.0) and is certified strictly positive by dual independent Arb ball arithmetic evaluations: Path 1 (direct completed xi with Simpson remainder <= 1.14e-8 and real-line tail envelope <= 7.16e-12) yielding [0.023172204, 0.023172227], and Path 2 (decomposed A+P with finite Dirichlet sum N=50000 and L^2(W) majorant tail bound <= 0.002265) yielding [0.0209073, 0.0254375]. Zero is strictly excluded (0 notin X_{xi, W}), proving that exact cross-term cancellation fails for this fixed Gaussian candidate instance.
